newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK to hold private talks on relaxing beef ban.
newsitem.headline: UK to hold private talks on relaxing beef ban.

text.p: Britain will not formally raise the question of exempting herds certified to be free of mad cow disease from a worldwide ban on British beef exports at next week's EU Farm Council, UK diplomats said on Friday.
But they added the issue would be discussed in private.
Exemptions to the ban were not on the official agenda, one diplomat said.

However, British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg and Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth were likely to sound out EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler's views on the scheme when they saw him privately on Monday.
"It's hard to imagine them not discussing BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) and the way forward," the diplomat said.
Technical discussions between British and Commission officials began two weeks ago on the definition of BSE-free herds and how the scheme would operate.
But progress was unlikely until after EU scientists had given their advice in mid-November on new British scientific studies casting doubt over a planned selective cull of cattle most at risk to BSE.
The cull was one of the conditions in a deal agreed by EU leaders in Florence in June for a gradual lifting of the seven-month-old British ban.
Exemption of certified herds would be a first step.
Transmittable spongiform encephalopathies will also be on the agenda of the next EU Health Council on November 12.
